## Setting
Dividing the utility bills. The five people in a shared house have been splitting gas, water, and electricity in a way that was agreed when only three of them lived there. They are deciding how the bills will be divided from now on. Participants: Victoria, Mio, Benjamin, Jonathan and Minato. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Electrician's quote for the rooms
- The last twelve utility statements
- Monthly settle observed at another house
- Trial run of a reconciliation template
- Kitchen notice about the cooler
- Winter habits at a house paying ahead
- Plug-in monitor readings room by room
- Sunlight and heating need by room
- Payment log for the last twelve months
- Settling up when the last rooms filled

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Benjamin, Mio, Jonathan, Victoria and Minato. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. | Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |

If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Participants
Name: Victoria
Age: 37
Gender: female
Personality: Victoria is a calm and rational person, but at times her excessive thoughtfulness can create barriers between her and those around her. She is reserved in her emotional expressions and keenly observes the expressions and attitudes of others, trying to discern their inner thoughts. Because she does not express herself much, she often gives others the impression of being somewhat mysterious, but deep down she has a strong will and a determination to stick to her beliefs. At times, she may display expressions of anxiety or fear, but it is precisely in such moments that her true strength becomes evident.
Concern: The utilities envelope has stopped bearing any relation to what I put aside for it, and in the cold months my share lands like a second rent. I do not want to commit to anything before I know what the money actually does across a year, and what changing the setup would cost us up front.

Name: Mio
Age: 17
Gender: female
Personality: Mio has a cheerful and energetic personality that naturally makes those around her smile. She is curious and loves to try new things. She can be a little clumsy at times, but people tend to laugh it off and forgive her when she makes mistakes. She has strong opinions of her own, but is also able to listen to the opinions of others, making her a well-balanced person.
Concern: Working out what everyone owes has quietly become a monthly job that lands on whoever is least able to say no, and it takes longer every time someone queries it. Whatever we settle on, somebody has to keep it running, and I want to know how much of their evenings it will really swallow.

Name: Benjamin
Age: 28
Gender: male
Personality: Benjamin is an intelligent and calm person. He is able to think calmly and rationally, and even in emotional situations, he places importance on logic. In public, he is elegant and polite, often incorporating sarcasm and humor into his conversations, but he is skilled at doing so without hurting others, creating a harmonious atmosphere. He also has an introverted side, often engrossed in deep thought, and occasionally keeps his distance from those around him. However, his calmness and knowledge are factors that earn him the trust of others even in difficult situations.
Concern: I have started doing arithmetic in my head before switching anything on, and last winter I sat here in a coat rather than be the one who turned the heating up. What we choose will quietly decide how this place feels to live in, and I would rather that were said aloud than discovered in February.

Name: Jonathan
Age: 38
Gender: male
Personality: Jonathan has a calm and introverted personality and values inner peace. He prefers spending quiet time alone rather than forming deep connections with others. As a result, he loves books and knowledge and reads frequently. When interacting with others, he is gentle and kind, occasionally flashing an unexpected smile. Though he exudes a mysterious and serene aura, he rarely shares personal details about himself with others. Those around him often find comfort in his quiet kindness and composed demeanor.
Concern: The way we divide this was worked out when the house was two-thirds full, and it now asks exactly the same of people whose days here look nothing alike. I keep hearing that somebody is carrying somebody else, and I would rather establish whether that is true than let it fester as a rumour.

Name: Minato
Age: 10
Gender: male
Personality: Minato has a calm personality and likes to interact with people around him in a peaceful manner. He is a little naive and sometimes has an expression that makes it difficult to understand what he is thinking, but his innocence makes him a soothing presence to those around him. He is very curious and shows interest in everything, especially learning new things. He is highly sensitive and sensitive to the feelings of others, but he is not good at asserting himself and sometimes has difficulty expressing his opinions.
Concern: Money has started to sour how we speak to each other here: a reminder gets read as an accusation, and whoever sends it is avoided for a week afterwards. I would rather look squarely at where the bills have already damaged things between us than keep smoothing it over.

## Hidden information
The options and the full text of every card are listed here. The participants do not know them before the schedule above says so, and nothing from them may appear in the talk before the round in which it is revealed.

Options (see the schedule above):
- A: Flat Household Share. The total is divided by the number of residents each month, with the amount recalculated whenever someone moves in or out of the house.
- B: Seasonal Fixed Rate. A set monthly figure is agreed in advance for each season, and the difference against the actual bills is settled once at the end of the year.
- C: Per-Room Metering. Individual meters are fitted to the private rooms, and each person settles their own reading while the shared-area consumption is billed to the household as a whole.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Electrician's quote for the rooms: An electrician came to look and quoted 34,000 yen a room to fit sub-meters, plus a 3,000 yen check on each every year and two days of wiring.
- The last twelve utility statements: The last twelve statements, laid out side by side, show February at 29,400 yen and August at 9,100, with no two consecutive months landing within 4,000 yen of each other.
- Monthly settle observed at another house: Sitting in on the monthly settle at a share house that meters its rooms showed forty minutes of logging readings, issuing five demands, and splitting the corridor and kitchen total by hand.
- Trial run of a reconciliation template: A year-end reconciliation template trialled on the house's own figures meant keying in every invoice from the year one by one, then computing five refunds or top-ups separately.
- Kitchen notice about the cooler: A notice about the cooler went up in the house's kitchen in July and stayed all summer; two people said they sweated it out rather than have a pooled bill argued over.
- Winter habits at a house paying ahead: In a household paying a figure fixed ahead for each season, nobody prices a switch before flicking it; they said the hall heater simply stayed on through January.
- Plug-in monitor readings room by room: A plug-in monitor moved between the rooms, a week in each, found the heaviest drawing roughly four times the lightest, most of that a heater and a desktop left running.
- Sunlight and heating need by room: Two of the five rooms take no direct sun and need heat from November, while the south pair stay warm into December; the rooms were originally handed out by lot.
- Payment log for the last twelve months: The house's payment log shows three of the last twelve months settled more than a fortnight late, each time after somebody queried why the amount asked of them had moved again.
- Settling up when the last rooms filled: When the last two rooms filled up mid-month, it took three weeks to agree what the newcomers owed for the days before they arrived, and part was written off.

## Setting
Dividing the utility bills. The five people in a shared house have been splitting gas, water, and electricity in a way that was agreed when only three of them lived there. They are deciding how the bills will be divided from now on. Participants: Victoria, Mio, Benjamin, Jonathan and Minato. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Electrician's quote for the rooms
- The last twelve utility statements
- Monthly settle observed at another house
- Trial run of a reconciliation template
- Kitchen notice about the cooler
- Winter habits at a house paying ahead
- Plug-in monitor readings room by room
- Sunlight and heating need by room
- Payment log for the last twelve months
- Settling up when the last rooms filled

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Benjamin, Mio, Jonathan, Victoria and Minato. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. | Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |

Name: Victoria
Age: 37
Gender: female
Personality: Victoria is a calm and rational person, but at times her excessive thoughtfulness can create barriers between her and those around her. She is reserved in her emotional expressions and keenly observes the expressions and attitudes of others, trying to discern their inner thoughts. Because she does not express herself much, she often gives others the impression of being somewhat mysterious, but deep down she has a strong will and a determination to stick to her beliefs. At times, she may display expressions of anxiety or fear, but it is precisely in such moments that her true strength becomes evident.
Concern: The utilities envelope has stopped bearing any relation to what I put aside for it, and in the cold months my share lands like a second rent. I do not want to commit to anything before I know what the money actually does across a year, and what changing the setup would cost us up front.

Name: Mio
Age: 17
Gender: female
Personality: Mio has a cheerful and energetic personality that naturally makes those around her smile. She is curious and loves to try new things. Age: 28
Gender: male

Age: 38
Gender: male
Personality: Jonathan has a calm and introverted personality and values inner peace. He prefers spending quiet time alone rather than forming deep connections with others. Age: 10
Gender: male
